ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the point $(-3,-1)$ and the point $(4,-6)$ are on two sides of the line $3 x-2 y-a=0$, then the range of values of $a$ is ( )
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read from the problem statement the two points P=(-3,-1), Q=(4,-6), and the line equation is 3x-2y-a=0. Let the function on the left side of the line be F(x,y)=3x-2y-a. Substituting P gives F(P)=3×(-3)-2×(-1)-a=-9+2-a=-7-a. Substituting Q gives F(Q)=3×4-2×(-6)-a=12+12-a=24-a. The two points are on opposite sides of the line, which is equivalent to F(P) and F(Q) having opposite signs, so (-7-a)(24-a)<0. The two critical values of this inequality are a=-7 and a=24, and checking shows that the product is less than 0 between the two, therefore -7<a<24.
